guide.title: Quick start
guide.description: Follow these 4 steps in order. This page guides the setup, but it cannot automatically confirm plugin installation, Gateway restarts, or tool visibility inside a remote OpenClaw session.
guide.intro: MindAtlas owns the capability catalog, knowledge data, and execution runtime. OpenClaw owns the chat entry, tool registration, and conversation orchestration. After installation, the plugin also ships the overview, auto-capture, retrieval, and summary MindAtlas skills. `mindatlas-overview` is the main router, and the actual callable tools still come from the live MindAtlas capability catalog. In practice, the agent should route from the session-visible `mindatlas_*` tool surface first, not from an imaginary in-session catalog tool. Follow the sequence on this page from top to bottom: generate the secret, expose catalog items, install the plugin, paste the config, restart the Gateway, then verify one live call from a fresh session.

plugin.title: Install and configure the plugin on the OpenClaw host
plugin.description: Run the commands below on the machine that runs the OpenClaw Gateway, paste the config, and validate it before you restart anything.
plugin.hostHint: Run every command in this step on the OpenClaw Gateway host. This page cannot execute those commands for you.

details.install: Install the plugin from the MindAtlas repository on the same machine that runs OpenClaw. If OpenClaw runs on another server, copy the `integrations/openclaw-mindatlas` folder there first. The install command itself does not require `baseUrl` or `integrationSecret` yet, and you do not need to install the 4 shipped skills separately because they are bundled with the plugin and synced into OpenClaw on Gateway start. Running `configure:skills` writes `skills.load.extraDirs` for the shipped skills and warns if it finds legacy MindAtlas `tools.allow` or `tools.profile` remnants.
details.baseUrl: Set `plugins.entries.openclaw-mindatlas.config.baseUrl` to the MindAtlas backend or reverse-proxy origin that the OpenClaw host can really reach, then paste the bearer secret generated on this page into `integrationSecret`. The shipped skills guide routing, but the actual exposed tools still depend on the session-visible MindAtlas capability surface.
details.refresh: Catalog availability changes can be picked up by the plugin refresh cycle. If a tool name, exported title, exported description, or input schema changes, active sessions will not hot-refresh. Start a new session or reload the OpenClaw Gateway or plugin. If a session shows no `mindatlas_*` tools, the agent should say MindAtlas is not exposed in that session instead of silently falling back to generic memory.

verify.title: Verify from a fresh OpenClaw session
verify.description: Restart the Gateway with your own deployment method, open a brand-new OpenClaw session, and check that the session no longer says MindAtlas tools are missing.

guide.installTitle: Install the plugin on the OpenClaw host
guide.installDescription: These commands are meant to be run where your OpenClaw Gateway is installed. The plugin package lives in this MindAtlas repository, and installation also brings in the 4 shipped MindAtlas skills that the plugin syncs into OpenClaw on startup. A new session is still required before the refreshed skill and tool surface appears in prompts.

locate.title: Locate the MindAtlas repository or plugin folder
locate.description: Open a shell on the OpenClaw machine and enter the MindAtlas repository root. If OpenClaw is deployed on another machine, copy the `integrations/openclaw-mindatlas` folder there first.

install.title: Install the shipped plugin and sync the bundled skills
install.description: Install the native `openclaw-mindatlas` plugin from the local filesystem, then run `configure:skills` on the same host. This step does not require the final plugin config yet.

verify.title: Confirm the plugin is visible to OpenClaw
verify.description: Check that OpenClaw can see the newly installed plugin before you continue with configuration. After the later Gateway restart, the plugin will sync the shipped skills and register tools from the current MindAtlas catalog.

guide.configTitle: Fill in the OpenClaw plugin configuration
guide.configDescription: Find the active OpenClaw config file, paste the plugin block below, replace the placeholders, and validate it before you restart the Gateway.

findConfig.description: Run this first if you are not sure which config file your OpenClaw installation is using.

guide.configExampleDescription: Replace `baseUrl` with the MindAtlas backend address that OpenClaw can access, and replace `integrationSecret` with the secret generated on this page.
guide.restartDescription: After the config validates, restart the OpenClaw Gateway with your own deployment method. Then open a fresh session because active sessions do not hot-refresh `mindatlas_*` tools or bundled skills.

notes.catalogOnly: OpenClaw only sees catalog items that are currently exposed. Hidden or currently unavailable items should not appear as callable tools, and a session with no visible `mindatlas_*` tools cannot route MindAtlas work automatically.
notes.skillBoundary: The 4 shipped skills tell OpenClaw when it should call MindAtlas and which class of capability to prefer. `mindatlas-overview` is the broad router, while summary, retrieval, and auto-capture are narrower sub-strategies. The actual callable tools still come only from the currently exposed MindAtlas capability catalog.
notes.refresh: After creating, deleting, or editing catalog items, refresh the catalog on the OpenClaw side. If a tool name, exported title, exported description, or input schema changes structurally, active sessions still will not hot-refresh, so start a new session or reload the Gateway or plugin as well. If startup registration fails or a previously unavailable tool becomes available later, fix the issue and reload the Gateway because the plugin no longer late-registers tools after startup. If the current session still shows no MindAtlas tools, the agent should say MindAtlas is not exposed in that session instead of silently substituting generic memory.
